_meta.purpose: Trigger evals for the SKILL.md description. A query passes when the skill is loaded exactly as should_trigger expects, measured as a trigger rate over N runs.
_meta.split_policy: Fixed at 12 train / 8 validation (60/40). Never optimize against the validation set — it exists only to detect overfitting. Keep the split stable across iterations so runs are comparable.

how_to_read_failures.should_trigger_false: Description too narrow. It should fire on structure decisions (where does this file go, what files does this feature need), not only on the words 'architecture' or 'refactor'.
how_to_read_failures.should_trigger_low_rate: Nondeterminism. Re-run before editing the description.
how_to_read_failures.should_not_trigger_true: Description too broad. Laravel Boost already covers framework usage — queries, deployment, packages, queue config. This skill should not load for those.

known_risks: P4 ('add login') is the highest-value trigger: the wrong answer is to write a LoginController over Fortify. It must fire to prevent that.
P5 and P11 mention validation only, no architecture vocabulary. They test whether the dual-validation half of the description fires on its own.
N1 and N5 are Laravel questions that Boost answers better. If these start triggering, the description has drifted toward 'anything Laravel'.
N6 and N8 are infrastructure and other-framework asks, included to catch a description that fires on 'queue' or 'validation' as bare nouns.
